chapter_theme: Praise (தோத்திரம்): the Lord pervades the elements, the lights, the worlds and souls, is great beyond the gods' measure and small within the flesh, yet is found within the body and in his devotees' hearts; his feet are every heaven, and naming and praising him cut away deeds, desire and the sea of births.
structure_note: Devotional verses of the speaker's own seeking and finding (2982 to 2999), with a short linked chain in which each verse begins with the last word of the one before (2992 to 2995), then a run of verses on the Lord's pervasion of elements, lights and worlds and his being beyond them (3000 to 3024), ending with a riddle verse (3025).

2982.reading: Those who drove the long chariot of the mind in search of the elusive one went off without knowing the land and lament; I, having wandered through countries and lands, found our treasured Lord within the land of the body.
2982.nuance: மாயன் is usually Vishnu, but here may simply mean the elusive one whom seekers chase. காயம் (body) is the key word: the search outward fails and the find is within. காயம்மின் is odd; it may be காயம் with an emphatic or a misdivided word, and some take மின் as the flash of light seen within.

2983.reading: If you ask who sat on the mountain-like rutting elephant while sweet music was sung, know from the songs that they were those who had recited the name of the First One of the time before.
2983.nuance: The verse promises honour, pictured as a royal elephant ride with music, to those who repeat the Lord's name. Later tradition might see Sundarar's ride to Kailasa on a white elephant here, but that would make the verse later than Tirumular is usually placed; read it as a general image.

2984.reading: They say of me, crying out because I cannot see the Father, the pearl of pearls, the young budding sun, the Lord whom all the gods praise: 'this one is a madman'.
2984.nuance: பித்தன் (madman) is also a name of Siva himself, so the devotee mocked as mad shares a name with the Lord he longs for. The verse turns on longing for one not seen (காணாது அரற்றுகின்றேன்).

2985.reading: Our holy form has entered and stays; our knower who knows has entered and stays; he has entered and stays in the hearts of his devotees; it is the one who entered and stays that I praise.
2985.nuance: புகுந்துநின்றான் (entered and stays) opens every line. போதறிவாளன் may mean the one who knows the right time, or the one whose knowledge is pure awareness.

2986.reading: He has not entered the mirror of the elements, yet he is there in awareness; in the mirror of the Veda he appears otherwise; in the mirror of justice he is in the minds of those who think of him; in the mirror of song I heard him and stood.
2986.nuance: கண்ணாடி (mirror) structures the verse: the elements do not reflect him, the Veda shows him in a different form, right conduct and thought hold him, and song lets him be heard. போதுளன் may mean 'he is in awareness' or 'he is in the flower' (of the heart); both are traditional.

2987.reading: Recite the Lord's thousand names and you will be held within a thousand protections; those who can perform a thousand fire offerings have seen their thousand desires and are done with them.
2987.nuance: ஏமம் is protection or delight. கண்டொழிந்தார் can mean they saw their desires through and were done with them, or that they saw desire and left it; the plain promise is release from desire by naming and offering.

2988.reading: I praise, and praising I make known the renowned knowledge; I make sure the red feet of the Lord of the mind; I proclaim Siva-yoga, hear it; I praise, calling him our Lord.
2988.nuance: அறையோ is a call for attention, as a crier's or a challenge's. The four verbs (போற்று, தேற்று, சாற்று, போற்று) frame the work as a teacher's proclamation as well as a devotee's praise.

2989.reading: Seek Nandi in many ways: passing through the lotus of the flesh and beyond it, coming back after the heavenly world has worshipped, you may drink honey to your fill and be sated.
2989.nuance: ஊனார் கமலம் (lotus of the flesh) is traditionally a centre of the yogic body and தேன் (honey) the nectar the yogi tastes. A plain devotional reading also stands: seek him by every means and the sweetness comes.

2990.reading: The rare treasure has come and stands for his devotees; even if Indra and the other gods ask for him, he is beyond the sky of space, and they get nothing but the sound of beautiful women.
2990.nuance: The contrast is between devotees, to whom he comes, and the gods, whose pleasures (the clamour, துழனி, of heavenly women) are all they have. The construction of line 3 is loose and the reading is a guess.

2991.reading: Like water muddied by earth, people muddied in their thoughts do not say 'this is the Lord'; Siva is the one who scoops from the pond within, sets the mud to one side, and makes the water clear.
2991.nuance: The image is of clearing muddy water: the mind is the pond, and the Lord does the settling. உண்ணிற் குளம் (the pond within) is read as the inner mind; the phrasing of line 3 is compressed.

2992.reading: To one who longs for the one of true penance he is like a gooseberry come into the palm; seeking the pure one, the Father of the gods who stood as the pure way, I have settled and come to rest.
2992.nuance: கைத்தலம் சேர் நெல்லிக்கனி (a gooseberry in the hand) is proverbial for what is plainly seen and surely held. அமைந்தொழிந்தேன் (I settled and ceased) opens the chain of linked verses that follows.

2993.reading: I have settled; I have been made complete in a knowledge of measureless renown; there is no wavering at all; the holy one, coming near the smoking earth, is the bountiful one who apportions and gives.
2993.nuance: தடுமாற்றம் ஒன்றில்லை (no wavering) states the settled state. புகைந்தெழும் பூதலம் (the earth rising in smoke) is obscure: it may be the earth as the burning ground, or the world of distress.

2994.reading: The bountiful chief, lord of the good heavenly land, first of the Veda with flood-water in his matted hair, wondering whether the deceitful will see him, hides within the heart and rules there.
2994.nuance: கள்ளப் பெருமக்கள் (deceitful folk) are those with hidden guile; the Lord hides from them, yet rules from within the heart. The verse may also play on the Lord as himself the hidden thief of hearts.

2995.reading: Those who worship daily the God who gave his ruling flower-feet stand in goodness; I have laid with my mind the sword of the lord who cuts away the planets and deeds.
2995.nuance: கோள் (the planets, their bad influence) and வினை (deeds) are what the Lord cuts. வாளும் மனத்தொடும் வைத்தொழிந்தேன் can mean that I set his sword in my mind, or that I laid down my sword and my mind before him in surrender.

2996.reading: For those who can praise his feet with effort: if they desire it, his feet are the heroes' heaven; if they join them, the world of merit; if they are reformed, the holy water too.
2996.nuance: The feet stand in for every reward promised elsewhere: the heaven of warriors fallen in battle, the world earned by merit, and the bathing places that wash away sin. வருந்தி (with effort, with longing) qualifies the praise.

2997.reading: He who cut through the heavens is in this world a solitary teacher with no house of his own; I have held to the light, sweet as a drink, that comes within as one eats the forest plantain fruit.
2997.nuance: போதகன் (teacher) and தானகம் இல்லா (with no dwelling of his own) suggest the Lord as a wandering teacher. கானக வாழைக்கனி and பானகச் சோதி (a light like a sweet drink) are images of sweetness taken within; their exact reference is not clear.

2998.reading: That is the destiny where the gods above dwell; that is the place where the flowing Ganga is; that praise removes the clinging of old deeds; that place, having seized them, is also the end.
2998.nuance: பதி may be a holy place (some think of Kasi on the Ganga) or the Lord himself, which the word also means in Siddhanta. Line 4 (வவ்விட்டது அந்தமும்) is obscure.

2999.reading: Above are the gods, below the great ascetics, below them humans in distress; the one whose fragrant matted hair wears the bilva garland does all this and is my dear life.
2999.nuance: Line 2 (மாதுஅனங் கானது) is broken and could not be read; the ranking of beings above and below is the plain outline. The last line makes the Lord the life of the speaker's life.

3000.reading: He whose throat swallowed the poison of the encircling dark sea is the Lord unborn in the seven and the two; he is there in the lute, the spring and the forest, and is also the king who lives in the seven and five.
3000.nuance: ஏழும் இரண்டும் and எழுந்தைந்து are counts (seven and two; seven and five) whose referents, worlds or regions or tattvas, the verse does not fix.

3001.reading: The First Lord is like the world and the earth, like the high wind, like the fire of spreading rays, like the water of the great clouds, and like their passing away again: he is the lord of the gods of the directions.
3001.nuance: The list runs through the elements: earth, wind, fire and water, with செலவு (going) perhaps standing for space or for dissolution. ஒத்து (being like) is weaker than 'being': the verse compares rather than identifies.

3002.reading: Knowing the right manner, he is there as fire and sun; knowing it, he is there as the Lord in the wind; knowing it, as the great moon; and knowing the manner of knowledge, that is how he spreads that land.
3002.nuance: பரிசறிந்து (knowing the manner) opens each line. The last line is compressed; பாரிக்கும் may mean spreads out or sustains.

3003.reading: Even beyond the end he stands as each thing that is; in the bound world he is the great treasure of those below; the Supreme himself pervades all the worlds he gave: this is the glory of his coming to create.
3003.nuance: பந்த உலகு (the bound world) and கீழோர் (those below) suggest bound souls, for whom he is the treasure. அதுஅதுவாய் நிற்கும் (stands as each thing) is a phrase of pervasion that Siddhanta reads as indwelling rather than identity.

3004.reading: Though the three eggs and the two eggs are his crown, the Father's form is said to be the seven worlds, and his red feet reach as far as the underworld; the intoxicated do not know this and rejoice in it.
3004.nuance: முத்தண்ண ஈரண்டம் (three and two world-eggs) is a cosmological count that cannot be fixed here. மத்தர் (the intoxicated, the deluded) are those who miss the cosmic form.

3005.reading: The First Lord, our Lord, Lord of light of the wide world, stands as the light of the three lights; the First Lord is beyond the cosmos and below it; the First Lord stands in the middle.
3005.nuance: சுடர் மூன்று (the three lights) are traditionally sun, moon and fire. ஆதிப்பிரான் (the First Lord) opens three of the four lines.

3006.reading: He is great, rising high beyond the cosmos, and small in a birth beyond the body; each time his servants see the ringing anklet that walked, he stands as the pure way, hanging there for them.
3006.nuance: The pairing of பெருமையன் and சிறுமையன் (great and small) is the point, as in 3024. பிண்டம் கடந்த பிறவிச் சிறுமையன் and தூங்கிநின்றான் (stood hanging, or stood intent) are hard to fix.

3007.reading: The Lord, whose roving gaze is ringed by the great sea, has filled the whole land; he first created all its strength, and stands as the whole field of the senses in golden colour.
3007.nuance: உலவுசெய் நோக்கம் (the roaming gaze) and புலம் (the field, or the senses) are uncertain; பலம் may be fruit or strength.

3008.reading: As the supreme and the lower through many aeons, as the Supreme bearing this wide world, people do not grasp how he stood as bearer of the earth; he stands full as one who needs no support.
3008.nuance: The verse plays on -பரன்: பராபரன் (supreme and lower), தராபரன் (bearer of the earth) and நிராபரன் (without support, or without ornament).

3009.reading: The great god who is praised is he alone, there is no other; he is the force and the sound and the subsiding of sound; he is always the body that is other too; that is the great god; the Lord stands mingled as the breath.
3009.nuance: ஓசை ஒடுக்கம் (the subsiding of sound) may point to the resolution of nada in yoga. வேற்றுடல் (the other body) is obscure. காற்று (wind, breath) is taken as the life-breath.

3010.reading: If all the directions are Siva, he alone, there is no need, men, to say anything more; as all smoke gathers outside in fire, all buds are our First Lord.
3010.nuance: The image of smoke and fire in line 3 is unclear: it may mean that every rising thing goes back to its source in the Lord. முகை (bud) may stand for all that is yet to unfold.

3011.reading: He spread out, the seven wide worlds becoming one; he stands so that one may say 'this is he' and yet is not easily had; Siva himself, becoming many, many souls, is also the trusted one who spoke and lives in the world.
3011.nuance: சிவன்தான் பலபல சீவனுமாகி (Siva himself becoming many souls) sounds like identity of the Lord and souls. Siddhanta tradition takes such lines as his pervading souls without being one with them; both readings stand on the words.

3012.reading: Seek the chief who stands beyond the three kalas, the lord of the tattvas; he has no price; even speaking with the gods there are no words for him; he is the one who dwells within.
3012.nuance: கலை ஒரு மூன்றும் (the three kalas) may be the kalas of sun, moon and fire or three of the five kalas of Siddhanta cosmology; the verse does not say.

3013.reading: Cutting the bond made by Brahma of the earth, cutting the attachment to smallness made by the tall one, removing the deeds done in thicket-like penance, he saved me his servant and took me in love.
3013.nuance: நெடியான் (the tall one) is Vishnu; Brahma's bond is taken as birth and Vishnu's as attachment to sustained life. செடியார் தவம் (penance thick as a thicket) may be austerities that themselves bind; the verse says the Lord removes even these.

3014.reading: The eight directions moved crying 'Lord'; the unfailing one rises as sound from sound; there one land and its nine rich regions: he dwells in them as fragrance in a flower.
3014.nuance: ஓசையில் நின்றெழு சத்தம் (sound rising from sound) may refer to nada; செழுங்கண்டம் ஒன்பதும் (the nine regions) is a traditional division of the earth.

3015.reading: Our Lord is neither non-existent nor existent; his vision splits open the good heart; ancient, pure, unshaken, a pure gem, the light beyond words, he stands, continuing.
3015.nuance: இல்லனும் அல்லன் உளன் அல்லன் (not non-being, not being) places him beyond both categories. நெஞ்சம் பிளந்திடும் காட்சி (a vision that splits the heart) is overwhelming sight.

3016.reading: The thief-chief called 'I', within the heart where it subsides and outside too, and Nandi of the fragrant matted hair: for those who proclaim the greatness of his bounty, he has cut through the sea of mire.
3016.nuance: நானெனும் கள்ளத் தலைவன் (the thief-chief called I) is read as the ego. அள்ளற் கடல் (the sea of mire) is taken as the sea of births or of sin. The syntax joining the ego and Nandi in lines 1 and 2 is unclear.

3017.reading: The gods and the asuras, opposed to each other, every day recount and seek his ringing anklet; he wells up within their hearts and outside, and, making them distinct, there becomes the light of a lamp.
3017.nuance: வேறுசெய்து (making distinct) may mean that he separates them from their bonds or that he stands apart from them; the verse does not settle it.

3018.reading: He is not the open space that came in the sky, yet has a form; not an object that came to the eye, yet is seen; not the fruit that came from melody, yet of its nature: our Lord is bliss beyond reckoning.
3018.nuance: Each line denies a sensory category and then grants the Lord a likeness to it (மேனியன், காட்சியன், பான்மையன்).

3019.reading: The highest one, the great sea that delights everywhere, of pearl's light and of blue-black, the siddhas and gods think on the Lord through all time and still do not know him fully.
3019.nuance: தேர்ந்தறியார் (they do not know by searching) sets even the siddhas and the gods short of him.

3020.reading: As many colours as there are, so is the Lord; as many virtues, so much joy; as many wrongs, so much sin; though people see many outward things, they do not praise him.
3020.nuance: மறம் here is the opposite of அறம் (wrongdoing), not valour. The middle lines pair virtue with joy and wrong with sin as if to measure them one for one.

3021.reading: He stood here, he stood there: where is he? He rose up, the lord of the worlds, the holy one; he stood in the night as the sun and the great moon; the Lord stands everywhere like rain.
3021.nuance: The verse answers its own question (எங்குளன், where is he) with the rain, which falls on every place.

3022.reading: What perceives is the breath, being the highest; what perceives our Lord is subtle knowledge; what joins him is breath, and is slight; he stands as perception, body and cosmos.
3022.nuance: வாயு (breath) and நுண்ணறிவு (subtle knowledge) are both named as means of knowing; the yogic sense of breath as what reaches the Lord is traditional. புல்லியதாயும் (being slight, or clinging) is uncertain.

3023.reading: By his own strength he bore the seven worlds; by his own strength he is lighter than the atom; by his own strength he leans on none of the eight mountains; by his own strength he is the wide sea.
3023.nuance: தன்வலியால் (by his own strength) opens every line: nothing holds him up, while he holds all. The eight mountains are the traditional mountains at the quarters that bear the earth.

3024.reading: Though our Lord is great beyond all others, he is there mingled within the flesh in smallness too; the great god is not of the measure the gods know; he himself knows the measure of penance.
3024.nuance: The last line can be read as 'he alone knows how much penance is done' or 'he is known only in the measure of one's penance'.

3025.reading: The great sprout risen from the seed of the banyan of the body: in the pot-like body the horse has ripened; the senseless fools ate it, and caught within the body they quarrel.
3025.nuance: This is a riddle verse in the style of Tirumular's hidden-meaning songs. பிண்டாலம் (body-banyan), குண்டாலம் and குதிரை (horse, perhaps the breath or the mind) cannot be fixed; the plain sense is only that fools caught in the body consume its fruit and quarrel.

links.note: 1823 makes the body of flesh the temple and the heart the shrine; 2982 tells the same as a story of search: those who chased the Lord across lands lost him, and the speaker found him in the body.
Both end on the same phrase, புகுந்துநின்றான்: in 27 the Lord enters the minds of those who bow to Nandi daily, in 2985 he enters and stays in his devotees' hearts.
Both make the Lord's thousand names (ஆயிர நாமம்) a practice: 34 praises them going and sitting, 2987 promises protection and the end of desire to those who recite them.
The Kural says the two kinds of deed do not cling to those devoted to the Lord's praise; Tirumular says the lord whom the worshipper keeps in mind cuts away deeds and the planets' sway.

If அள்ளற் கடல் is the sea of births, the two verses agree: the Kural's sea of births is crossed by those who reach the Lord's feet, and Tirumular's sea of mire is cut for those who proclaim his bounty.
Both set the Lord beyond those who would know him: in 13 Vishnu, Brahma and the gods cannot measure him, in 3019 the siddhas and gods think on him through all time without knowing him.
Both end with the Lord as rain: in 11 Nandi is the rain-pouring cloud, in 3021 the Lord is everywhere like rain, answering the question of where he is.

10 lists the Lord as bearer of the earth, fire, sun, moon, mountain and sea, ending தடவரை தண்கடலாமே; 3023 repeats the frame, ending தடம்கடலாமே, but grounds each line in his own strength and adds that he is lighter than an atom.

source_issues: 2999 line 2 (தானிடர் மானுடர் கீழது மாதுஅனங் கானது) is broken in its word division and may be corrupt.
2998 line 4 (பதியது வவ்விட்டது அந்தமும் ஆமே) and 3025 (பிண்டாலம், குண்டாலம், குதிரை) are obscure and may be corrupt.
2982 line 4 (காயம்மின்) and 3001 line 1 (ஒத்ததஉயர், with a doubled syllable) look misdivided or misprinted.
